rule: docs/TREE_PLAN.md: one yard tree for every two or three houses, in back yards and at lot corners, never against a fence or a wall (zone 813 -> about 400)
written: by hand, 19 Nov 2026 (cloud session, the city-wide superchecker run from the bottom of the list). The quadrant's twenty-two builder trees go (a row of torrey pines, corals and queen palms every 6 m along the back fences, jacarandas and a coral by the seating, three on the open lawn); seven come back on their own spots, about one for every two houses: by the picnic table, the grill, the beach umbrella, on the open lot corner, and two in back yards.

trees.why: the shared back lawn with the picnic table and the shade sail: a magnolia beside them
the same lawn 23 m east, 13 m from any wall: the lawn's second tree
the big open lot corner, 35 m from the walls: one norfolk pine, a landmark seen from the street
the back yard with the gas grill (1.5 m off): a jacaranda over the cook
the next yard by the closed beach umbrella: a jacaranda over the lounging spot
the east back yard, 6.5 m from the house: the yard's tree
the west end of the south back fence row, 5.3 m from the house: the row's one tree
